subject: csl
general_outcomes: By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
Participate and respond to issues in the community for mutual benefit and learning at the local, national, regional and global levels as a responsible citizen.
Cultivate respect and appreciation of diversity in communities for harmonious living within the broader community.
Demonstrate ability to apply life skills, financial literacy skills, use resources prudently and establish sustainable social enterprises for mutual social and economic wellbeing.
Develop and apply research skills for the transformation of self and community.
Act with integrity, care for others and contribute to the progress of humanity while upholding desirable values.
Appreciate the role of Community Service Learning in addressing pertinent and contemporary issues in the community.

substrands.name: Self-Awareness in the Community

substrands.name: Introduction to Action Research
learning_outcomes: explain the meaning of action research
analyse the characteristics of action research
illustrate the cycle of action research
use action research cycle to address issues in the community
appreciate action research in addressing challenges in the community.
learning_experiences: use digital devices or print materials to find the meaning of action research
discuss the meaning of action research as it applies in problem solving

using digital devices or print materials to search for the characteristics of action research (Reflection, continuous, factual, visible, practical and interesting) and illustrate them for class presentation
illustrate the cycle (plan, act, observe, reflect) of action research and present in class
brainstorm on the importance of action research while appreciating the diverse perspectives shared
review case studies on action research projects addressing community issues
identify and discuss the phases, cycles, and characteristics used in each case study
collaborate to design a mock action (role play, simulation) research project focused on solving a community issue
present the project plan to the class, explaining how the characteristics, phases, and cycles of action research are applied
discuss the importance of action research in solving community issues and share
listen to a resource person or a podcast or watch a video on how to effectively conduct action research
create posters to raise awareness about what action research is and its importance in solving community issues
• reflect on the role of action research in addressing issues in the community
Suggested learning experiences
inquiry_questions: How can you apply action research to address an issue in the community?
Key Inquiry Questions
core_competencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner thinks critically as they analyse case studies to determine the principles, phases and cycles.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner design a poster to create awareness on what action researches us and its importance in solving community issues.
Communication and Collaboration: Learner work together with others to design a mock action research and present the action research.
values: Unity: Learners work as part of a group to model a mock action research where they will display team spirit.
Responsibility: Learners proactively participate in designing a mock action research as they engage in assigned roles and those of others
pertinent_issues: Social Awareness Skill as learners use effective communication during discussions and presentation activities

substrands.name: Problem identification
learning_outcomes: critique given scenarios to identify the problem in a community
use data collection tools to record the characteristics of the problem identified
analyse simple data to determine the nature and extent of the problem
document and manage data for information dissemination
appreciate the importance of accurate documentation for effective problem resolution.
learning_experiences: work in small groups to identify a problem from a scenario by applying problem identification techniques discussed in class
design and use simple data collection tools to document problems highlighted from the scenario, (observation tools, tally tools, online forms and checklists.)
conduct simple analysis of the data collected by counting and tallying from the class scenarios
present their analysed data using varied media including digital devices
prepare summary reports on observations using various formats and multimedia and present
manage data collection, handling, organisation analysis and reporting while maintaining integrity
demonstrate mutual co existence while participating in reflection activities to draw lessons from the class activity
use digital devices to document and manage the data for sharing. The data can also be stored manually through filing.
Suggested learning experiences
inquiry_questions: How can effective problem identification help in addressing real life issues in the community?
Key Inquiry Questions
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: Learners speak engagingly and clearly as they present their analysed data.
values: Integrity: Learners display honesty in exhibiting integrity in data handling-collection, organisation analysis and reporting
pertinent_issues: Social cohesion: Learners demonstrate mutual co-existence while participating in reflection activities to draw lessons from the class activity.

substrands.name: Implementation Process
learning_outcomes: identify a viable solution to address a community problem
create an implementation plan focusing on the identified solution
implement the plan to address the identified problem
develop a reflective report on the implemented action
appreciate the process of
designing solutions to address challenges in the community.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on potential solutions to the identified problem within the school community
accommodate divergent opinions when discussing proposed solutions by evaluating the required time, human and financial resources, scope, and potential impact
engage in class dialogue, consultation, and voting to determine the most viable solution to the problem
work in project teams to design a detailed implementation plan (timeline, milestones, resource allocation, personnel responsibilities, reporting templates,)
carry out the implementation activities in teams by collecting
data using checklists, observations, tallies, and trend analysis, and by holding reflective meetings to review progress
conduct reflection activities to review the process, progress and identify areas of improvement
reflect and link how the activities have enhanced learning to appreciate the benefits of CSL.
share the reports digitally or in print format (charts, posters, videos, audio visual presentations, the school website, and school social media pages)
Suggested learning experiences
inquiry_questions: How can we implement a comprehensive project plan and ensure continuous improvement through reflective practices?
Key Inquiry Questions
core_competencies: Digital Literacy: Learners use digital devices to share reports using charts, posters, videos, audio visual presentations, the school website, and school social media pages.
values: Respect: Learners accommodate divergent opinions when discussing each proposed solution.
Unity: Learners display team spirit while designing a detailed project.
